## Birch Path {#birch-path}

Named by [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), the Birch Path is a picturesque, narrow, and spicy-aired pathway fringed with young birches and wildflowers that winds through Mr. Bell's woods on the route to the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P70](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0070), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P0](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER XV. > On her thirteenth birthday, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) walks to school with [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) and discusses growing up, her creative story writing, and a new plan to form a story club with their friends. Later, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) tells [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) about the success and rules of the story club, though [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) remains skeptical of the endeavor.
>
> — v1 · CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed

## Bright River {#bright-river}

Bright River is a location reachable by an eight-mile drive from [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) Cuthbert's home, featuring a train station house with a long platform and ladies' waiting room, as well as a small local hotel.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P12](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0012), [v1 CHAPTER I. > [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) travels to Bright River station expecting to pick up an orphan boy, only to discover that a young girl has been left for him instead. Unable to tell the talkative child about the mistake, [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) takes her bag and offers her a ride to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) in his buggy. During the initial leg of the drive, the girl talks continuously about her vivid imagination and dramatic thoughts, while [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) finds himself surprisingly enjoying her conversation.
>

## Green Gables {#green-gables}

Green Gables is the secluded, meticulously kept homestead of [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) and [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), situated at the edge of their cleared land in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), reachable by a long, rose-bordered lane, and featuring an orchard-embowered house and a very neat yard.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER I. **Associated with:** [Jerry](../character/jerry.md), [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md)

> [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) discovers her missing brooch caught in a black lace shawl and realizes Anne's false confession was fabricated just to be allowed to go to the picnic. Apologetic for doubting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) sends her off to the event with Jerry driving, and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) later returns home delighted after a wonderful day.
>

[Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) explains that [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) has gone to [Bright River](../codex/places.md#bright-river) to pick up an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia) to help on the farm.
